cleaned_text: Meesho IPO share allotment is likely to be finalised later tonight, December 8, after the issue drew an investor demand of 79 times in the primary market. The Rs 5,421-crore Meesho IPO was open for subscription from December 3-5. The company had fixed the price band at Rs 105-111 per share. IPO applicants can check their Meesho IPO allotment status on the official website of the registrar, KFin Technologies Limited, by entering their application number or PAN. The status will also be available on the BSE and NSE websites. Step 1 Open the direct link to the registrar on this URL Step 2 Select the IPO from the dropdown menu. Step 3 Investors can check the allotment status by filling in details like PAN, Application number or DP client ID. Step 4 Press the Submit button Step 5 The allotment status will be shown in the window. Step 1 Open the website of NSE by clicking on this direct link Step 2 Select the company Meesho by selecting Equity SME IPO bid details Step 3 Investors can check the allotment status by filling in details like their IPO Application number or PAN details after selecting company symbol. Step 4 Press the Submit button Step 5 The allotment status will be shown in the window. Step 1 Open the website of BSE by clicking on this direct link Step 2 Select Equity in the issue type. Step 3 Fill in the required details including the Issue Name. Step 4 Enter PAN number and click on Search to view the status Step 5 The allotment status will be shown in the window. According to platforms tracking the grey market activities, the shares of Meesho are commanding a GMP of 38 percent in the unregulated market. Investorgain quoted a GMP of Rs 42 for the shares of the company, indicating a listing gain of 37.84 percent. Meanwhile, IPO Watch quoted a higher GMP of 42 percent for shares of the company. Meesho IPO shares will be listed on both NSE and BSE platforms on December 10. Title: Gold price today: Rates flat as investors await US Fed rate decision; Check 24K, 22K, 18K prices in your city
Content: Spot gold price stood at $4,207 an ounce on December 8, as of 6:05 a.m IST, which is a recovery of around 0.29 percent up in the last 24 hours. India’s December gold futures closed the Friday trade at Rs 1,30,419 per 10 grams of 24-carat purity, which is 0.033 percent down from previous close. Meanwhile, the rupee stood at 89.945 against the U.S. dollar on December 6. Interest rate traders now comprise 88.4 percent vote for the probability of a 350-375 target rate bps in the upcoming U.S Federal Reserve meeting come December 9, as per FedWatch data that tracks the probabilities of changes to the Fed rate. The Indian Bullion and Jewellers Association (IBJA) announced the price of yellow at Rs 1,28,592 for 10 grams of 999 purity in their 18:30 p.m rate session on December 5.  Gold rates across India’s major cities showed remarkable uniformity, with only marginal differences due to local taxes, jeweller margins, and logistics costs.  Augmot report published on December 5 stated that gold and silver prices are consolidating as rising US Treasury yields counteract support from a weaker dollar, while investors await the Federal Reserve’s policy stance ahead of its December meeting. “Gold is holding firm today as a softer US dollar ahead of the Federal Reserve meeting underpin investor interest. While rising US Treasury yields are acting as a headwind, the dollar’s weakness continues to support bullion demand. As long as gold stays resilient near key support levels of 1,28,200, safe-haven demand remains intact, investors seem to be pricing in a favourable macro outlook,” said Rahul Gupta, Chief Business Officer, Ashika Group. The Augmont Bullion report published on December 5, stated that gold has started its upward journey again; the next target is $4,300 (Rs 132,000) and $4,345 (Rs 133,500) with strong support at $4200 (Rs 129,000).

Title: Corona Remedies IPO subscribed 27% on Day 1 so far, retail portion booked 41%; check latest GMP
Content: The initial public offering of Corona Remedies opened for public subscription today, December 8. The maiden issue of the pharma company has been subscribed 27 percent so far on Day 1. The IPO received bids for 12.24 lakh shares, as against the offer size of 45.72 lakh shares, according to data on NSE at 12 pm. Retail investors have booked 41 percent of their reserved portion, while Non-Institutional Investors (NII) have subscribed 28 percent of their allotted quota. Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIB) are yet to make any substantial bid for the IPO. Ahead of listing, the unlisted shares of Corona Remedies were trading with more than 27 percent grey market premium over the IPO price, according to data on Investorgain and IPO Watch. This has fallen from the 34 percent GMP quoted by the sites on Friday. However, the grey market estimates still signal a strong listing for the company. Corona Remedies launched its IPO today to raise more than Rs 655 crore through an entirely offer for sale (OFS) of shares with no fresh issue component. This means that all of the IPO proceeds will go the selling investors and not the company. The price band for the IPO has been set at Rs 1,008-1,062 per share. Investors can bid for a minimum of 14 shares, requiring an investment of Rs 14,868 per lot, and in multiples thereafter. The IPO will remain open for public bidding between December 8 and December 10. The allotments are likely to be finalized by December 11, and the shares are scheduled to be listed on stock exchanges BSE and NSE on December 15. Corona​‍​‌‍​‍‌​‍​‌‍​‍‌ Remedies IPO is entirely an offer-for-sale, which means that the market will look at the issue solely from a fundamental perspective, that is how strong the margins are, how deep the product portfolio is, and how consistent the growth is, said Siddharth Maurya, Founder & Managing Director, Vibhavangal Anukulakara Pvt. Ltd. "The company boasts a decent presence in the leading therapeutic areas, however, its profit figures are lower than those of some of its competitors," the analyst said. He added that investors should position this offering as one in the pharma sector that will generate steady returns over time instead of that which can bring quick ​‍​‌‍​‍‌​‍​‌‍​‍‌profits. cleaned_text: The initial public offering of Corona Remedies opened for public subscription today, December 8. The maiden issue of the pharma company has been subscribed 27 percent so far on Day 1. The IPO received bids for 12.24 lakh shares, as against the offer size of 45.72 lakh shares, according to data on NSE at 12 pm. Retail investors have booked 41 percent of their reserved portion, while Non-Institutional Investors NII have subscribed 28 percent of their allotted quota. Qualified Institutional Buyers QIB are yet to make any substantial bid for the IPO. Ahead of listing, the unlisted shares of Corona Remedies were trading with more than 27 percent grey market premium over the IPO price, according to data on Investorgain and IPO Watch. This has fallen from the 34 percent GMP quoted by the sites on Friday. However, the grey market estimates still signal a strong listing for the company. Corona Remedies launched its IPO today to raise more than Rs 655 crore through an entirely offer for sale OFS of shares with no fresh issue component. This means that all of the IPO proceeds will go the selling investors and not the company. The price band for the IPO has been set at Rs 1,008-1,062 per share. Investors can bid for a minimum of 14 shares, requiring an investment of Rs 14,868 per lot, and in multiples thereafter. The IPO will remain open for public bidding between December 8 and December 10. The allotments are likely to be finalized by December 11, and the shares are scheduled to be listed on stock exchanges BSE and NSE on December 15. Corona Remedies IPO is entirely an offer-for-sale, which means that the market will look at the issue solely from a fundamental perspective, that is how strong the margins are, how deep the product portfolio is, and how consistent the growth is, said Siddharth Maurya, Founder Managing Director, Vibhavangal Anukulakara Pvt. Ltd. The company boasts a decent presence in the leading therapeutic areas, however, its profit figures are lower than those of some of its competitors, the analyst said. He added that investors should position this offering as one in the pharma sector that will generate steady returns over time instead of that which can bring quick profits. Follow all IPO news here.

Title: Persistent Systems CEO says AI not a bubble, chipmakers in a 'supercycle'; outlines long-term growth path
Content: Sandeep Kalra, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director at Persistent Systems, believes the current wave of Artificial Intelligence is not a speculative bubble; rather, the chipmakers are in 'more of a supercycle'. Speaking with CNBC TV18 on the occasion of its 26th anniversary, Kalra differentiated between the underlying technology's long-term impact and market valuations, providing a detailed outlook on how AI will reshape various sectors and drive growth for IT services firms. He argued that while valuations are a separate discussion, the technology itself is transformative. Kalra outlined a multi-tiered view of the AI ecosystem's beneficiaries. In the short to medium term, he identified chip manufacturers like Nvidia, AMD, and Google, along with ecosystem supporters like Broadcom, as the 'biggest gainers.' He noted their strong order books, which are filled for the next one to two years, are a testament to the immense investment in data centre infrastructure. For hyperscalers such as Microsoft, Google, and AWS, Kalra pointed out that while they are investing hundreds of billions in capital expenditure, they are also actively monetising this through AI cloud services, developer tools, and co-pilots, creating real revenue and profitability. For technology services companies like Persistent Systems, Kalra sees them as 'winners in the longer run.' He argued that possessing the technology is only one part of the equation. The real value for enterprises lies in integrating AI into their specific contexts, building new business use cases, and developing new business models, all of which require significant system integration activity. Currently, he said many enterprises are in the initial stages, focusing on getting their data ready for AI consumption, a space where Persistent is already seeing larger programs. Looking ahead, Kalra projected a significant revenue shift for the IT services industry. While AI-related projects may currently account for single-digit revenue, he forecasts that in three to five years, AI-native work could constitute '30 to 40% or more' of revenues for such companies. He clarified that this is a multi-year journey, not a short-term projection for the next few quarters. He also touched upon 'agentic AI' as a more advanced stage that is still in its infancy and will require robust, enterprise-wide data integration. When asked about the impact of the depreciating Indian rupee, Kalra acknowledged that there would be a short-term currency impact. However, he downplayed its overall significance, calling it a 'smaller enabler' for the industry. He emphasised that the Indian IT industry's success is built on more than just currency fluctuations. Kalra pivoted back to his central theme, stating that the most critical factor for the next three to five years is for companies to build strong capabilities in AI, which he believes will provide a 'significant amount of tailwind' for the industry. He declined to offer specific forward-looking guidance on margins, citing the company's silent period during the quarter.

cleaned_text: Sandeep Kalra, Chief Executive Officer and Executive Director at Persistent Systems, believes the current wave of Artificial Intelligence is not a speculative bubble rather, the chipmakers are in more of a supercycle. Speaking with CNBC TV18 on the occasion of its 26th anniversary, Kalra differentiated between the underlying technologys long-term impact and market valuations, providing a detailed outlook on how AI will reshape various sectors and drive growth for IT services firms. He argued that while valuations are a separate discussion, the technology itself is transformative. Kalra outlined a multi-tiered view of the AI ecosystems beneficiaries. In the short to medium term, he identified chip manufacturers like Nvidia, AMD, and Google, along with ecosystem supporters like Broadcom, as the biggest gainers. He noted their strong order books, which are filled for the next one to two years, are a testament to the immense investment in data centre infrastructure. For hyperscalers such as Microsoft, Google, and AWS, Kalra pointed out that while they are investing hundreds of billions in capital expenditure, they are also actively monetising this through AI cloud services, developer tools, and co-pilots, creating real revenue and profitability. For technology services companies like Persistent Systems, Kalra sees them as winners in the longer run. He argued that possessing the technology is only one part of the equation. The real value for enterprises lies in integrating AI into their specific contexts, building new business use cases, and developing new business models, all of which require significant system integration activity. Currently, he said many enterprises are in the initial stages, focusing on getting their data ready for AI consumption, a space where Persistent is already seeing larger programs. Looking ahead, Kalra projected a significant revenue shift for the IT services industry. While AI-related projects may currently account for single-digit revenue, he forecasts that in three to five years, AI-native work could constitute 30 to 40% or more of revenues for such companies. He clarified that this is a multi-year journey, not a short-term projection for the next few quarters. He also touched upon agentic AI as a more advanced stage that is still in its infancy and will require robust, enterprise-wide data integration. When asked about the impact of the depreciating Indian rupee, Kalra acknowledged that there would be a short-term currency impact. However, he downplayed its overall significance, calling it a smaller enabler for the industry. He emphasised that the Indian IT industrys success is built on more than just currency fluctuations. Kalra pivoted back to his central theme, stating that the most critical factor for the next three to five years is for companies to build strong capabilities in AI, which he believes will provide a significant amount of tailwind for the industry. He declined to offer specific forward-looking guidance on margins, citing the companys silent period during the quarter.

Speaking with CNBC TV18, Drew Pettit, Director of US Equity Strategy ETF Analysis Strategy Research at Citi, outlined his firm's global market strategy, highlighting an overweight position on select emerging markets and a neutral stance on India. "Our economists and team expect 25 basis points, I believe at the next four meetings after December," he stated. The central question, according to Pettit, is whether these cuts will be accompanied by economic weakness or if the US economy will remain resilient. He suggested that the index could close the year somewhere between 6,600 and 7,000, potentially threatening Citi's bull case scenario of 7,000. However, the primary engine for their EM preference is the opportunity to gain exposure to growth and Artificial Intelligence (AI) at a reasonable valuation. While acknowledging the strong and unchanged growth narrative, Pettit believes the positive outlook is already reflected in the country's valuations. "You have priced in a really good earnings and growth backdrop for India, so it remains neutral to us," he said. He also touched upon India's significant underperformance relative to the broader EM basket this year, attributing it partly to currency weakness, which he links to perceived tariff risks. He noted that for global macro traders, the currency often acts as the first "relief valve" for such concerns.

cleaned_text: With the US Federal Reserves next policy meeting on the horizon, the market has largely priced in a 25 basis point rate cut, but the key focus remains on the path of future cuts and the resilience of the US economy. Speaking with CNBC TV18, Drew Pettit, Director of US Equity Strategy ETF Analysis Strategy Research at Citi, outlined his firms global market strategy, highlighting an overweight position on select emerging markets and a neutral stance on India. Pettit noted that while a rate cut in the upcoming meeting is expected, the more critical factor for markets is the trajectory of monetary policy into the next year. Our economists and team expect 25 basis points, I believe at the next four meetings after December, he stated. The central question, according to Pettit, is whether these cuts will be accompanied by economic weakness or if the US economy will remain resilient. A scenario where the economy holds up despite rate cuts would signify a soft landing, which could broaden market participation beyond mega-cap growth stocks into cyclical sectors where earnings growth might improve. Looking at the SP 500, which has already seen a 12% gain year-to-date, Pettit believes strong sentiment is likely to persist through the typically low-volume end-of-year trading period. He suggested that the index could close the year somewhere between 6,600 and 7,000, potentially threatening Citis bull case scenario of 7,000. Contrary to some assumptions, Pettit clarified that Citis global strategy is currently overweight on Emerging Markets EM. This is complemented by an overweight position on Europe excluding the UK as a cyclical play with potential for inflecting growth. However, the primary engine for their EM preference is the opportunity to gain exposure to growth and Artificial Intelligence AI at a reasonable valuation. EM is actually a way to get growth and AI exposure at a pretty reasonable price, and we lead the overweight in EM with China and South Korea, Pettit explained. He pointed to companies like Alibaba, Tencent, SK Hynix, and Samsung as examples of firms that screen well in their AI at a reasonable price basket. Regarding India, Citi maintains a neutral stance. While acknowledging the strong and unchanged growth narrative, Pettit believes the positive outlook is already reflected in the countrys valuations. You have priced in a really good earnings and growth backdrop for India, so it remains neutral to us, he said. He also touched upon Indias significant underperformance relative to the broader EM basket this year, attributing it partly to currency weakness, which he links to perceived tariff risks. He noted that for global macro traders, the currency often acts as the first relief valve for such concerns.

Title: IndiGo flight chaos to persist today, warns Delhi airport amid slow operational recovery
Content: Flight delays linked to IndiGo’s ongoing operational crisis are expected to continue on Monday, Delhi airport cautioned in an advisory issued early in the day. The airport authority urged travellers to verify their flight status before leaving for the terminal, noting that schedules remain unstable as the airline works to restore normal operations. Passenger Advisory issued at 06:30 Hours#DelhiAirport#PassengerAdvisory#DELAdvisorypic.twitter.com/hrpGxn7Oxr — Delhi Airport (@DelhiAirport) December 8, 2025 “IndiGo flights may continue to experience delays. Passengers are advised to check the latest flight status with their airline before heading to the airport to avoid any circumstances,” the advisory said. IndiGo’s nationwide operational crisis has continued to ripple across India, with thousands of passengers still facing cancellations, delays, missing baggage and pending refunds. Over six days, the airline cancelled more than 2,000 domestic and international flights, triggering widespread chaos at major airports. The airline said it has so far processed Rs 610 crore in refunds and delivered around 3,000 pieces of delayed baggage. On Sunday, IndiGo operated about 1,650 of its scheduled 2,300 flights, while roughly 650 remained cancelled. The carrier has announced automatic refunds for cancelled bookings and waived change and cancellation fees for travel between December 5 and 15. Meanwhile, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has granted a one-time 24-hour extension to IndiGo’s Accountable Manager and CEO to reply to the show-cause notice issued on December 6 over large-scale disruptions and alleged non-compliances. The officials sought additional time citing operational constraints linked to the scale of the airline’s network and multiple factors behind the disruptions. After reviewing the request, the DGCA extended the deadline only until 6 pm on December 8 and warned that no further extensions would be granted. Failure to submit a comprehensive response, the regulator said, would result in the case being decided ex parte. The show-cause notice, issued to CEO Pieter Elbers, accused the airline of “significant lapses in planning, oversight and resource management” and a failure to adequately prepare for new Flight Duty Time Limitations (FDTL) norms. The DGCA said this amounted to prima facie non-compliance with the Aircraft Rules, 1937, and related crew duty and rest regulations. The regulator also flagged shortcomings in passenger care, noting that IndiGo did not provide mandatory assistance to those affected by cancellations and delays, in violation of passenger rights norms. As disruptions persisted on Sunday, over 400 flights were cancelled, IndiGo said it expects to stabilise operations by December 10. CEO Pieter Elbers said the airline is “recovering from the disruption” and plans to operate around 1,650 flights as it adapts to the impact of the revised FDTL rules. Major hubs, including Hyderabad, Kolkata and Delhi, saw the highest cancellations as thousands of passengers remained stranded or awaiting refunds.

cleaned_text: Flight delays linked to IndiGos ongoing operational crisis are expected to continue on Monday, Delhi airport cautioned in an advisory issued early in the day. The airport authority urged travellers to verify their flight status before leaving for the terminal, noting that schedules remain unstable as the airline works to restore normal operations. Passenger Advisory issued at 0630 HoursDelhiAirportPassengerAdvisoryDELAdvisorypic.twitter.comhrpGxn7Oxr Delhi Airport December 8, 2025 IndiGo flights may continue to experience delays. Passengers are advised to check the latest flight status with their airline before heading to the airport to avoid any circumstances, the advisory said. IndiGos nationwide operational crisis has continued to ripple across India, with thousands of passengers still facing cancellations, delays, missing baggage and pending refunds. Over six days, the airline cancelled more than 2,000 domestic and international flights, triggering widespread chaos at major airports. The airline said it has so far processed Rs 610 crore in refunds and delivered around 3,000 pieces of delayed baggage. On Sunday, IndiGo operated about 1,650 of its scheduled 2,300 flights, while roughly 650 remained cancelled. The carrier has announced automatic refunds for cancelled bookings and waived change and cancellation fees for travel between December 5 and 15. Meanwhile, the Directorate General of Civil Aviation DGCA has granted a one-time 24-hour extension to IndiGos Accountable Manager and CEO to reply to the show-cause notice issued on December 6 over large-scale disruptions and alleged non-compliances. The officials sought additional time citing operational constraints linked to the scale of the airlines network and multiple factors behind the disruptions. After reviewing the request, the DGCA extended the deadline only until 6 pm on December 8 and warned that no further extensions would be granted. Failure to submit a comprehensive response, the regulator said, would result in the case being decided ex parte. The show-cause notice, issued to CEO Pieter Elbers, accused the airline of significant lapses in planning, oversight and resource management and a failure to adequately prepare for new Flight Duty Time Limitations FDTL norms. The DGCA said this amounted to prima facie non-compliance with the Aircraft Rules, 1937, and related crew duty and rest regulations. The regulator also flagged shortcomings in passenger care, noting that IndiGo did not provide mandatory assistance to those affected by cancellations and delays, in violation of passenger rights norms. As disruptions persisted on Sunday, over 400 flights were cancelled, IndiGo said it expects to stabilise operations by December 10. CEO Pieter Elbers said the airline is recovering from the disruption and plans to operate around 1,650 flights as it adapts to the impact of the revised FDTL rules. Major hubs, including Hyderabad, Kolkata and Delhi, saw the highest cancellations as thousands of passengers remained stranded or awaiting refunds.

Title: PC Jeweller shares rise on announcing fresh collaboration in Uttar Pradesh; check details
Content: PC Jeweller shares rose on Monday after the company announced a new collaboration aimed at supporting goldsmiths in Uttar Pradesh. The stock was up nearly 1 percent on Monday, trading at Rs 11.14 on the NSE at around 11: 30 a.m. The shares were seen 2.17 per cent higher at Rs 11.29, it's intraday high. In a statement, the Delhi-based company said it has partnered with the CM Yuva Udyami Yojana to help 1,000 PM Vishwakarma-certified goldsmiths (Sunar) in the first phase. The initiative seeks to enable these artisans in rural and semi-urban parts of Uttar Pradesh to become jewellery entrepreneurs and organised retail partners. PC Jeweller said the tie-up will offer support in branding, design, modern retail practices, digital skills and market linkages. The company added that the programme is expected to cover more than 5,000 such artisans across the country. According to the firm, over 85,000 PM Vishwakarma-certified goldsmith artisans are currently verified nationwide. PC Jeweller operates about 50 stores across India.

cleaned_text: PC Jeweller shares rose on Monday after the company announced a new collaboration aimed at supporting goldsmiths in Uttar Pradesh. The stock was up nearly 1 percent on Monday, trading at Rs 11.14 on the NSE at around 11 30 a.m. The shares were seen 2.17 per cent higher at Rs 11.29, its intraday high. In a statement, the Delhi-based company said it has partnered with the CM Yuva Udyami Yojana to help 1,000 PM Vishwakarma-certified goldsmiths Sunar in the first phase. The initiative seeks to enable these artisans in rural and semi-urban parts of Uttar Pradesh to become jewellery entrepreneurs and organised retail partners. PC Jeweller said the tie-up will offer support in branding, design, modern retail practices, digital skills and market linkages. The company added that the programme is expected to cover more than 5,000 such artisans across the country. According to the firm, over 85,000 PM Vishwakarma-certified goldsmith artisans are currently verified nationwide. PC Jeweller operates about 50 stores across India.

Title: Bajaj Finserv sets sight on Rs 21,000–24,000 crore profit by FY30
Content: Bajaj Finserv has unveiled a bold long-range plan for 2026–2030, targeting a consolidated profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 21,000–Rs 24,000 crore by FY30, implying an 18–22 per cent compound annual growth rate (CAGR) from current levels. According to a presentation made by Sanjiv Bajaj, Chairman and Managing Director, at BFS’ “Investor Day 2025” conference, this translates into the company’s consolidated assets rising to Rs 3.1–3.4 lakh crore by FY30, up from Rs 1.30 lakh crore in FY2025. It is also targeting over 220 million active customers from over 100 million now. These targets reflect a broader ambition, according to the presentation: to evolve from being a collection of standalone financial businesses into a truly integrated “financial services supermarket,” covering lending, insurance (life & general), wealth/asset management, and newer verticals, all under the Bajaj Finserv umbrella. A key enabler of this long-term goal, according to Bajaj, is the planned full acquisition of the insurance ventures. In March 2025, Bajaj Finserv signed agreements with Allianz SE to acquire its 26 percent stake each in the group’s life and general insurance joint ventures -- Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance Company (BALIC) and Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company (BAGIC) -- for Rs 24,180 crore. This transaction is expected to be completed by the early next calendar year. The divestment will give Bajaj Finserv “full control” over the insurance businesses, enabling the group to explore new strategic lines that were previously harder to pursue under a partnership structure. According to Bajaj, this opens up opportunities such as targeting NRIs via financial services in GIFT City, entering pension-fund management. Through GIFT City channels, GCC structures, and GN partnerships, Bajaj Finserv aims to extend its insurance-led ecosystem beyond India, especially into markets where motor, health and claims infrastructure remain fragmented or inefficient. By becoming a 100 percent owner, Bajaj Finserv expects to unlock synergies across businesses, aligning insurance, lending, wealth, and new financial services under one cohesive group strategy. Bajaj said he expects to evaluate a possible listing of at least some of the insurance arms within a 4–5 year window, meaning listing could happen as early as 2028 or slightly later. Bajaj Finserv also simultaneously plans a significant strategic reset across its insurance businesses as it prepares for full ownership following Allianz’s exit. The company will withdraw from loss-making geographies, wind down manpower-heavy distribution models, and scale back underperforming Insurance Marketing Distributors (IMDs). Instead, the focus will shift toward profitable segments such as commercial lines, high-margin protection-led life insurance, disciplined motor and health underwriting, and products with strong persistency and long-term value. This reorientation is aimed at improving combined ratios and creating a more stable, predictable earnings base for the insurance verticals, the presentation said. A major overhaul of the distribution architecture is also underway. Bajaj Finserv plans to pivot toward low-cost, scalable channels by expanding its agent and bancassurance networks, building Global Capability Centres (GCCs) for cross-border operations, and establishing Global Network (GN) partnerships to support international expansion. Digital channels will play a larger role, with deeper integration across the group’s ecosystem and its 16 crore–plus retail customer base. The company aims to leverage this vast pool of customer data to enable more refined segmentation, personalised offerings, and higher cross-sell penetration across insurance, health, and wealth products. Product innovation will form another key pillar of the strategy. The insurance businesses will integrate more closely with the group’s health and digital platforms, enabling bundled offerings that combine health services with insurance, hybrid protection-health products, SME-focused commercial insurance solutions, and future-ready pension-linked or annuity products once full consolidation is complete. These moves are intended to strengthen differentiation, widen customer reach and deepen engagement. In addition to the above, Bajaj Finserv plans to scale AI-driven underwriting, fraud detection, claims automation, particularly in motor and health, persistency analytics, and agent productivity tools. The group, according to the presentation, envisions a diversified “financial supermarket” spanning life and general insurance, lending, health and wellness services, asset and wealth management, digital financial marketplaces, alternative investment platforms, and pension and retirement solutions. Bajaj Finserv’s ambitious FY30 targets rest on its FY25 performance, according to the company’s Investor Day presentation, where its full-year consolidated income stood at Rs 1,33,822 crore, while consolidated profit after tax came in at Rs 8,872 crore. Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance reported an annual premium equivalent (APE) of Rs 6,317 crore and a value of new business (VNB) of Rs 1,152 crore, supported by strong growth in protection and annuity segments. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance recorded a gross written premium (GWP) of Rs 21,847 crore. Among emerging businesses, Bajaj Finserv Health Ltd., following its integration with Vidal Healthcare, posted Rs 892 crore in consolidated revenue. Meanwhile, Bajaj Finserv Direct Ltd., the group’s digital marketplace and services arm, turned “cash positive.” On the investments side, Bajaj Finserv Asset Management Ltd. (BFS AMC), launched only a few years ago, reported an AUM of Rs 20,365 crore as on March 31, 2025.

cleaned_text: Bajaj Finserv has unveiled a bold long-range plan for 20262030, targeting a consolidated profit after tax PAT of Rs 21,000Rs 24,000 crore by FY30, implying an 1822 per cent compound annual growth rate CAGR from current levels. According to a presentation made by Sanjiv Bajaj, Chairman and Managing Director, at BFS Investor Day 2025 conference, this translates into the companys consolidated assets rising to Rs 3.13.4 lakh crore by FY30, up from Rs 1.30 lakh crore in FY2025. It is also targeting over 220 million active customers from over 100 million now. These targets reflect a broader ambition, according to the presentation to evolve from being a collection of standalone financial businesses into a truly integrated financial services supermarket, covering lending, insurance life general, wealthasset management, and newer verticals, all under the Bajaj Finserv umbrella. A key enabler of this long-term goal, according to Bajaj, is the planned full acquisition of the insurance ventures. In March 2025, Bajaj Finserv signed agreements with Allianz SE to acquire its 26 percent stake each in the groups life and general insurance joint ventures -- Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance Company BALIC and Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company BAGIC -- for Rs 24,180 crore. This transaction is expected to be completed by the early next calendar year. The divestment will give Bajaj Finserv full control over the insurance businesses, enabling the group to explore new strategic lines that were previously harder to pursue under a partnership structure. According to Bajaj, this opens up opportunities such as targeting NRIs via financial services in GIFT City, entering pension-fund management. Through GIFT City channels, GCC structures, and GN partnerships, Bajaj Finserv aims to extend its insurance-led ecosystem beyond India, especially into markets where motor, health and claims infrastructure remain fragmented or inefficient. By becoming a 100 percent owner, Bajaj Finserv expects to unlock synergies across businesses, aligning insurance, lending, wealth, and new financial services under one cohesive group strategy. Bajaj said he expects to evaluate a possible listing of at least some of the insurance arms within a 45 year window, meaning listing could happen as early as 2028 or slightly later. Bajaj Finserv also simultaneously plans a significant strategic reset across its insurance businesses as it prepares for full ownership following Allianzs exit. The company will withdraw from loss-making geographies, wind down manpower-heavy distribution models, and scale back underperforming Insurance Marketing Distributors IMDs. Instead, the focus will shift toward profitable segments such as commercial lines, high-margin protection-led life insurance, disciplined motor and health underwriting, and products with strong persistency and long-term value. This reorientation is aimed at improving combined ratios and creating a more stable, predictable earnings base for the insurance verticals, the presentation said. A major overhaul of the distribution architecture is also underway. Bajaj Finserv plans to pivot toward low-cost, scalable channels by expanding its agent and bancassurance networks, building Global Capability Centres GCCs for cross-border operations, and establishing Global Network GN partnerships to support international expansion. Digital channels will play a larger role, with deeper integration across the groups ecosystem and its 16 croreplus retail customer base. The company aims to leverage this vast pool of customer data to enable more refined segmentation, personalised offerings, and higher cross-sell penetration across insurance, health, and wealth products. Product innovation will form another key pillar of the strategy. The insurance businesses will integrate more closely with the groups health and digital platforms, enabling bundled offerings that combine health services with insurance, hybrid protection-health products, SME-focused commercial insurance solutions, and future-ready pension-linked or annuity products once full consolidation is complete. These moves are intended to strengthen differentiation, widen customer reach and deepen engagement. In addition to the above, Bajaj Finserv plans to scale AI-driven underwriting, fraud detection, claims automation, particularly in motor and health, persistency analytics, and agent productivity tools. The group, according to the presentation, envisions a diversified financial supermarket spanning life and general insurance, lending, health and wellness services, asset and wealth management, digital financial marketplaces, alternative investment platforms, and pension and retirement solutions. Bajaj Finservs ambitious FY30 targets rest on its FY25 performance, according to the companys Investor Day presentation, where its full-year consolidated income stood at Rs 1,33,822 crore, while consolidated profit after tax came in at Rs 8,872 crore. Bajaj Allianz Life Insurance reported an annual premium equivalent APE of Rs 6,317 crore and a value of new business VNB of Rs 1,152 crore, supported by strong growth in protection and annuity segments. Bajaj Allianz General Insurance recorded a gross written premium GWP of Rs 21,847 crore. Among emerging businesses, Bajaj Finserv Health Ltd., following its integration with Vidal Healthcare, posted Rs 892 crore in consolidated revenue. Meanwhile, Bajaj Finserv Direct Ltd., the groups digital marketplace and services arm, turned cash positive. On the investments side, Bajaj Finserv Asset Management Ltd. BFS AMC, launched only a few years ago, reported an AUM of Rs 20,365 crore as on March 31, 2025.

Title: Wakefit IPO subscribed 7% on Day 1 so far, GMP signals decent listing: Should you apply?
Content: The initial public offering of Wakefit Innovations opened for public subscription today, December 8. The maiden issue of the popular mattress-maker has been subscribed 7 percent on Day 1 so far. The IPO received bids for nearly 27 lakh shares, as against an offer size of 3.63 crore shares, according to data on NSE at 11.30 am. Retail investors have booked 35 percent of their reserved portion, while Non Institutional Investors (NII) have subscribed 3 percent of the portion kept for them. Qualified Institutional Buyers (QIB) are yet to make any substantial bid for the IPO. Ahead of listing, the unlisted shares of the company were trading with 18.46 percent grey market premium (GMP) over the IPO price, according to data on Investorgain and IPO Watch. The grey market estimates signal towards a decent listing for the company. However, it is important to note that grey market is an unofficial market, and the actual listing may be significantly different from estimates. Wakefit Innovations launched its IPO to raise Rs 1,289 crore through a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 377 crore and an offer for sale of up to 4.7 crore shares worth Rs 912 crore. The price band for the IPO has been set at Rs 185-195 per share. Investors can bid for a minimum of 76 shares, requiring an investment of Rs 14,820 at the upper price band, and in multiples thereafter. The IPO will remain open for public bidding between December 8 and December 10. The allotments are likely to be finalized by December 11, and the shares are scheduled to be listing on stock exchanges BSE and NSE on December 15. Wakefit Innovations is strategically positioned to capitalize on the strong growth of India’s home and furnishings industry through its vertically integrated, omnichannel business model and extensive product portfolio spanning mattresses, furniture, and home décor, said Master Capital Services. The domestic brokerage noted that India’s home and furnishings market, which was valued at around Rs 3 trillion in 2024, is projected to grow to up to Rs 5.9 trillion by calendar year 2030, marking an 11-13 percent CAGR. This will be driven by organized retail expansion, online adoption, and premiumization. Master Capital Services said that within this category, India’s mattress market is projected to grow at a 10–12 percent CAGR by calendar year 2030, driven by rising awareness of sleep wellness and demand for branded, ergonomic products. “Investors may consider the IPO as a potential long-term investment opportunity,” it said. Wakefit's​‍​‌‍​‍‌​‍​‌‍​‍‌ IPO is a major step of the brand going beyond its digital roots and establishing a solid omnichannel presence, said Siddharth Maurya, Founder & Managing Director, Vibhavangal Anukulakara Pvt. Ltd. “While the rollout of branded stores could potentially lead higher revenue clarity, it also entails greater operational risks,” the analyst cautioned. With earning power ramping up and anchor engagement being robust, the stock may become attractive to investors with a long-term thesis on consumption growth instead of a short-term listing pop ​‍​‌‍​‍‌​‍​‌‍​‍‌play, Maurya said. cleaned_text: The initial public offering of Wakefit Innovations opened for public subscription today, December 8. The maiden issue of the popular mattress-maker has been subscribed 7 percent on Day 1 so far. The IPO received bids for nearly 27 lakh shares, as against an offer size of 3.63 crore shares, according to data on NSE at 11.30 am. Retail investors have booked 35 percent of their reserved portion, while Non Institutional Investors NII have subscribed 3 percent of the portion kept for them. Qualified Institutional Buyers QIB are yet to make any substantial bid for the IPO. Ahead of listing, the unlisted shares of the company were trading with 18.46 percent grey market premium GMP over the IPO price, according to data on Investorgain and IPO Watch. The grey market estimates signal towards a decent listing for the company. However, it is important to note that grey market is an unofficial market, and the actual listing may be significantly different from estimates. Wakefit Innovations launched its IPO to raise Rs 1,289 crore through a fresh issue of shares worth Rs 377 crore and an offer for sale of up to 4.7 crore shares worth Rs 912 crore. The price band for the IPO has been set at Rs 185-195 per share. Investors can bid for a minimum of 76 shares, requiring an investment of Rs 14,820 at the upper price band, and in multiples thereafter. The IPO will remain open for public bidding between December 8 and December 10. The allotments are likely to be finalized by December 11, and the shares are scheduled to be listing on stock exchanges BSE and NSE on December 15. Wakefit Innovations is strategically positioned to capitalize on the strong growth of Indias home and furnishings industry through its vertically integrated, omnichannel business model and extensive product portfolio spanning mattresses, furniture, and home dcor, said Master Capital Services. The domestic brokerage noted that Indias home and furnishings market, which was valued at around Rs 3 trillion in 2024, is projected to grow to up to Rs 5.9 trillion by calendar year 2030, marking an 11-13 percent CAGR. This will be driven by organized retail expansion, online adoption, and premiumization. Master Capital Services said that within this category, Indias mattress market is projected to grow at a 1012 percent CAGR by calendar year 2030, driven by rising awareness of sleep wellness and demand for branded, ergonomic products. Investors may consider the IPO as a potential long-term investment opportunity, it said. Wakefits IPO is a major step of the brand going beyond its digital roots and establishing a solid omnichannel presence, said Siddharth Maurya, Founder Managing Director, Vibhavangal Anukulakara Pvt. Ltd. While the rollout of branded stores could potentially lead higher revenue clarity, it also entails greater operational risks, the analyst cautioned. With earning power ramping up and anchor engagement being robust, the stock may become attractive to investors with a long-term thesis on consumption growth instead of a short-term listing pop play, Maurya said. Title: Small, midcap shares fall up to 7% amid profit booking; Kaynes Tech, Godrej Properties among top losers
Content: The small- and mid-cap shares came under sharp selling pressure on Monday as investors booked profits, dragging several stocks down by up to 7 percent and tracking weakness in the benchmark indices. The Nifty Smallcap100 index declined for the fifth straight session, slipping over 2 percent in intra-day trade. The index has fallen more than 4 percent over the past five sessions. Kaynes Technology India was the biggest loser in the Smallcap100 pack. The stock dropped 7.36 percent to Rs 320.5 on the NSE around 1 p.m. The counter extended losses after Kotak Institutional Equities flagged concerns over inconsistencies in the company’s related-party disclosures. JP Morgan advised investors against “bottom fishing” in the stock. Data Patterns (India) and Reliance Power were also among the major drags, declining 5.93 percent and 5.25 percent, respectively. Other notable losers included Poonawalla Fincorp, Aditya Birla Real Estate, Anant Raj, Deepak Fertilisers and Petrochemicals Corporation, and Ola Electric Mobility, which fell up to 5 percent. The Nifty Midcap100 index also slipped about 2 percent. Godrej Properties was among the top laggards, dropping 5.54 percent to Rs 115.30 on the NSE. Mahindra & Mahindra Financial Services, Bharat Dynamics, Housing & Urban Development Corporation and Prestige Estates Projects were also down as much as 5 percent. Broader market sentiment remained weak, mirroring declines in the Sensex and Nifty as investors turned cautious ahead of the US Federal Reserve’s policy meeting and continued foreign fund outflows. At around 12:30 p.m., the Sensex was down 458.52 points or 0.53 percent at 85,253.85. The Nifty slipped 170.80 points or 0.65 percent to 26,015.65.

Title: Govt to likely offload 1–2% LIC stake via offer for sale route in Q4FY26
Content: The government is examining a proposal to offload 1–2 percent stake in Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) through an offer for sale (OFS) in the fourth quarter (Q4) of the current financial year (FY26), with government sources citing the insurer’s large market capitalisation and subdued investor appetite as key considerations. A senior government source told Moneycontrol that the size of the LIC counter makes a larger sale difficult in the current environment. Earlier, government discussions had pointed to a larger 2.5–3 percent stake sale through an OFS. However, sources said current market conditions and muted investor appetite have prompted a revision to a smaller 1–2 percent tranche to ensure a successful execution. “A 1–2 percent LIC OFS is feasible and should fetch roughly Rs 13,000–14,000 crore. At this stage, there is simply no appetite for a 3 percent sale, which would be nearly Rs 24,000 crore,” the source said, adding that the sale is being aligned with broader market conditions. The official also noted that the government is watching global volatility, domestic flows, and institutional absorption capacity, before taking a final decision. “We are preparing for Q4, but the exact window will depend on how markets behave over the next several weeks,” the person added. If carried out, this would mark the first dilution of the Centre’s stake in LIC since the insurer’s landmark 2022 initial public offering (IPO). Since then, the government has not sold any further stake in the state-owned insurer. The government currently holds a 96.5 percent stake in LIC. The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) requires listed companies to have a 25 percent public shareholding, but granted LIC a special extension, allowing it until May 16, 2027, to reach a minimum 10 percent public stake, as it currently stands at 3.5 percent, post-IPO. This temporary 10 percent goal, set by Sebi's extension, is part of a longer, one-time exemption for LIC to eventually meet the full 25 percent norm by 2032. Investor activity in the broader market has seen a notable shift, especially among retail participants. Retail investors have offloaded over Rs 25,300 crore in equities in October–November 2025, driven by heightened volatility, profit-booking, and a preference for safer assets, even as domestic institutional investors and mutual funds continued to record net buying. This sharp reversal in retail flows has added to the government’s caution in timing the LIC OFS. Sources believe a staggered approach could prevent oversupply while still helping the government advance towards its disinvestment goals. “Investor sentiment has been fragile, particularly on the retail side. That is why a smaller tranche is safer and more practical in the current environment,” he said. Sources said a smaller, price-sensitive OFS could receive strong institutional demand, particularly from domestic funds, given the insurer’s weight in benchmark indices and its steady earnings profile. However, sustained global uncertainty and oil prices may keep foreign institutional investors cautious. The LIC counter, with a market capitalisation of roughly Rs 6 lakh crore, is among the largest PSU stocks. Any stake sale – particularly of this size – has the potential to influence market liquidity, index weightings, and short-term price movement. Given the government’s majority holding, periodic stake dilution is important for improving free float and enhancing long-term institutional participation. An offer for-sale is a mechanism through which promoters can sell shares to the public via the stock exchanges. The price is discovered through a bidding window typically open for a day. Retail investors may be allotted a portion at a discount, depending on the structure of the issue. OFS transactions help the government meet minimum public shareholding norms and raise funds without undertaking a full-fledged follow-on offer.

cleaned_text: The government is examining a proposal to offload 12 percent stake in Life Insurance Corporation of India LIC through an offer for sale OFS in the fourth quarter Q4 of the current financial year FY26, with government sources citing the insurers large market capitalisation and subdued investor appetite as key considerations. A senior government source told Moneycontrol that the size of the LIC counter makes a larger sale difficult in the current environment. Earlier, government discussions had pointed to a larger 2.53 percent stake sale through an OFS. However, sources said current market conditions and muted investor appetite have prompted a revision to a smaller 12 percent tranche to ensure a successful execution. A 12 percent LIC OFS is feasible and should fetch roughly Rs 13,00014,000 crore. At this stage, there is simply no appetite for a 3 percent sale, which would be nearly Rs 24,000 crore, the source said, adding that the sale is being aligned with broader market conditions. The official also noted that the government is watching global volatility, domestic flows, and institutional absorption capacity, before taking a final decision. We are preparing for Q4, but the exact window will depend on how markets behave over the next several weeks, the person added. If carried out, this would mark the first dilution of the Centres stake in LIC since the insurers landmark 2022 initial public offering IPO. Since then, the government has not sold any further stake in the state-owned insurer. The government currently holds a 96.5 percent stake in LIC. The Securities and Exchange Board of India Sebi requires listed companies to have a 25 percent public shareholding, but granted LIC a special extension, allowing it until May 16, 2027, to reach a minimum 10 percent public stake, as it currently stands at 3.5 percent, post-IPO. This temporary 10 percent goal, set by Sebis extension, is part of a longer, one-time exemption for LIC to eventually meet the full 25 percent norm by 2032. Investor activity in the broader market has seen a notable shift, especially among retail participants. Retail investors have offloaded over Rs 25,300 crore in equities in OctoberNovember 2025, driven by heightened volatility, profit-booking, and a preference for safer assets, even as domestic institutional investors and mutual funds continued to record net buying. This sharp reversal in retail flows has added to the governments caution in timing the LIC OFS. Sources believe a staggered approach could prevent oversupply while still helping the government advance towards its disinvestment goals. Investor sentiment has been fragile, particularly on the retail side. That is why a smaller tranche is safer and more practical in the current environment, he said. Sources said a smaller, price-sensitive OFS could receive strong institutional demand, particularly from domestic funds, given the insurers weight in benchmark indices and its steady earnings profile. However, sustained global uncertainty and oil prices may keep foreign institutional investors cautious. The LIC counter, with a market capitalisation of roughly Rs 6 lakh crore, is among the largest PSU stocks. Any stake sale particularly of this size has the potential to influence market liquidity, index weightings, and short-term price movement. Given the governments majority holding, periodic stake dilution is important for improving free float and enhancing long-term institutional participation. An offer for-sale is a mechanism through which promoters can sell shares to the public via the stock exchanges. The price is discovered through a bidding window typically open for a day. Retail investors may be allotted a portion at a discount, depending on the structure of the issue. OFS transactions help the government meet minimum public shareholding norms and raise funds without undertaking a full-fledged follow-on offer.

Title: Aequs IPO allotment: How to check status online via registrar, NSE & BSE; Check latest GMP
Content: Aequs IPO share allotment is likely to be finalised later tonight, December 8, after the issue drew a huge investor demand of a whopping 101.63 times in the primary market. The Rs 921.81-crore Aequs IPO was open for subscription from December 3-5. The company had fixed the price band at Rs 118-124 per share. IPO applicants can check their Aequs IPO allotment status on the official website of the registrar, KFin Technologies Limited, by entering their application number or PAN. The status will also be available on the BSE and NSE websites. Step 1: Open the direct link to the registrar on this URL (https://ipostatus.kfintech.com/). Step 2: Select the IPO from the dropdown menu. Step 3: Investors can check the allotment status by filling in details like PAN, Application number or DP client ID. Step 4: Press the Submit button Step 5: The allotment status will be shown in the window. Step 1: Open the website of NSE by clicking on this direct link (https://www.nseindia.com/products/dynaContent/equities/ipos/ipo_login.jsp). Step 2: Select the company 'Aequs' by selecting Equity & SME IPO bid details Step 3: Investors can check the allotment status by filling in details like their IPO Application number or PAN details after selecting company symbol. Step 4: Press the Submit button Step 5: The allotment status will be shown in the window. Step 1: Open the website of BSE by clicking on this direct link (https://www.bseindia.com/investors/appli_check.aspx) Step 2: Select Equity in the issue type. Step 3: Fill in the required details including the 'Issue Name'. Step 4: Enter PAN number and click on Search to view the status Step 5: The allotment status will be shown in the window. According to platforms tracking the grey market activities, the shares of Aequs are commanding a GMP of 32 percent in the unregulated market, according to IPO Watch. Aequs IPO shares will be listed on both NSE and BSE platforms on December 10.

cleaned_text: Aequs IPO share allotment is likely to be finalised later tonight, December 8, after the issue drew a huge investor demand of a whopping 101.63 times in the primary market. The Rs 921.81-crore Aequs IPO was open for subscription from December 3-5. The company had fixed the price band at Rs 118-124 per share. IPO applicants can check their Aequs IPO allotment status on the official website of the registrar, KFin Technologies Limited, by entering their application number or PAN. The status will also be available on the BSE and NSE websites. Step 1 Open the direct link to the registrar on this URL Step 2 Select the IPO from the dropdown menu. Step 3 Investors can check the allotment status by filling in details like PAN, Application number or DP client ID. Step 4 Press the Submit button Step 5 The allotment status will be shown in the window. Step 1 Open the website of NSE by clicking on this direct link Step 2 Select the company Aequs by selecting Equity SME IPO bid details Step 3 Investors can check the allotment status by filling in details like their IPO Application number or PAN details after selecting company symbol. Step 4 Press the Submit button Step 5 The allotment status will be shown in the window. Step 1 Open the website of BSE by clicking on this direct link Step 2 Select Equity in the issue type. Step 3 Fill in the required details including the Issue Name. Step 4 Enter PAN number and click on Search to view the status Step 5 The allotment status will be shown in the window. According to platforms tracking the grey market activities, the shares of Aequs are commanding a GMP of 32 percent in the unregulated market, according to IPO Watch. Aequs IPO shares will be listed on both NSE and BSE platforms on December 10.

Title: Buy ITC Hotels; target of Rs 250: ICICI Securities
Content: Established in 1975, with the first premium hotel launched in Chennai, the company’s hotels business represents one of India’s prominent branded hospitality chains, embodying the essence of Indian hospitality and sustainability. ITCHL is engaged in the business of owning, operating, managing and franchising hotels and resorts. As of Sep’25, the company operates 145+ hotels across 13,600+ keys with a mix of 41% owned and 59% managed keys across India, Sri Lanka and Nepal. It envisages reaching 220 operational hotels across 20,000+keys by 2030, with a mix of 33% owned and 67% managed keys. We initiate coverage with a BUY rating on ITCHL and a target price of INR 250. We value the company at a Dec’27E EV of INR 478.2bn – for its hotel business at 27x Dec’27E EV/EBITDA of INR 17.7bn at a 15% discount to our target multiple of 32x for Indian Hotels. Adding net cash of INR 30.6bn, as of Dec’27E, and Sri Lanka residential project NAV of INR 12.1bn, we derive an equity value of INR 520.9bn or INR 250/share. Title: IndiGo shares tumble 10%: Brokerages see costs rising for airline as FDTL norms trigger mass flight cancellations
Content: The shares of InterGlobe Aviation, the parent company of IndiGo, crashed nearly 10 percent on December 8, extending losses for the seventh consecutive session. Brokerages have cautioned investors, with some reducing their target prices for the stock as the airline continues to face massive disruptions. The shares of the company were trading at Rs 4,842.50 apiece in the afternoon hours of Monday, the lowest level seen by the stock in seven months. IndiGo’s flight cancellations continued to persist on Monday, leading to widespread chaos at India's major airports. Delhi airport issued an advisory in the early hours of the day, stating that schedules remain unstable as the airline works to restore normal operations. Over six days, the airline cancelled more than 2,000 domestic and international flights. Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA) has sent a show-cause notice to IndiGo CEO Peter Elbers over large-scale disruptions and alleged non-compliances. The show-cause notice, issued to CEO Pieter Elbers, accused the airline of “significant lapses in planning, oversight and resource management” and a failure to adequately prepare for new Flight Duty Time Limitations (FDTL) norms. A significant factor behind the chaos is a sharp shortage of crew, particularly pilots, following the introduction of revised Flight Duty Time Limitation (FDTL) norms last month. The new rules mandate more rest hours and humane rosters, but IndiGo has been struggling to realign its network accordingly. Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu today said that the IndiGo crisis was driven by problems in its crew rostering and internal planning system. Addressing the Rajya Sabha, Naidu said that strict Civil Aviation Requirements (CARs) are in place for passengers who have faced difficulties due to delays and cancellations. "I want more players in the industry. Today, India has a capacity of five big airlines and there has been an effort from the ministry to encourage more airlines," he added. UBS kept its 'Buy' call on the shares of IndiGo, but reduced its target price for the stock to Rs 6,350 per share. This implies an upside potential of more than 18 percent from the stock's previous closing price. The international brokerage said that inadequate preparations for the revised FDTL norms have led to major disruptions. It raised cost estimates for FY26-FY28 to account for the additional crew required to comply with the FDTL norms and higher operational costs driven by rupee depreciation against the dollar. IndiGo's long-term growth outlook however remains robust, supported by its international expansion, UBS said. It added that the key downside risks include any contingent costs arising from operational disruptions and further depreciation. Jefferies kept a 'Buy' call on the stock, with a target price of Rs 7,025 per share. This implies an upside potential of nearly 31 percent from the stock's previous closing price. The international brokerage noted that the company has been hit the hardest by the new FDTL norms, which reduce pilot duty hours and increases crew requirements. It noted that the rule change coincided with IndiGo’s capacity expansion, technical issues and congestion, triggering cascading disruptions. Airline is now recalibrating schedules and expects normalcy by mid-December, Jefferies noted, adding that IndiGo will face rising costs from disruptions and higher crew expenses. JM Financial kept a 'Reduce' call on the stock, with a target price of Rs 5,570 apiece. This implies an upside potential of around 4 percent from the stock's previous closing price. The domestic brokerage said that recent mismanagement leading to significant flight cancellations is largely a function of new FDTL norms impact kicking in immediately post Airbus software upgrade challenges. "The recent incident is likely to lead to a higher CAGR in CASK ex-fuel-ex-forex in future years subject to regulatory actions," it said. JM Financial noted that the show-cause notice sent to the CEO is likely to further dampen stock performance besides possible impending one-time penalty. “Near-term, we estimate earnings hit of 8-9% for FY26 if the situation lasts for a total of ~15 days. We await further clarity to revise our earnings estimates, given it’s a developing situation. Even as the FY26 earnings hit has been priced in, the stock is yet to price in 1) structural cost increase driven by regulatory actions 2) one time penalty 3) management change if any,” it added. IndiGo shares have fallen more than 13 percent in the past five days, and around 10 percent in the past one month. The shares of the airline have fallen more than 12 percent in the past six months, but are up nearly 9 percent in 2025 so far. The stock's P/E ratio currently stands at around 31. Brokerages have cautioned investors, with some reducing their target prices for the stock as the airline continues to face massive disruptions. The shares of the company were trading at Rs 4,842.50 apiece in the afternoon hours of Monday, the lowest level seen by the stock in seven months. IndiGos flight cancellations continued to persist on Monday, leading to widespread chaos at Indias major airports. Delhi airport issued an advisory in the early hours of the day, stating that schedules remain unstable as the airline works to restore normal operations. Over six days, the airline cancelled more than 2,000 domestic and international flights. Directorate General of Civil Aviation DGCA has sent a show-cause notice to IndiGo CEO Peter Elbers over large-scale disruptions and alleged non-compliances. The show-cause notice, issued to CEO Pieter Elbers, accused the airline of significant lapses in planning, oversight and resource management and a failure to adequately prepare for new Flight Duty Time Limitations FDTL norms. A significant factor behind the chaos is a sharp shortage of crew, particularly pilots, following the introduction of revised Flight Duty Time Limitation FDTL norms last month. The new rules mandate more rest hours and humane rosters, but IndiGo has been struggling to realign its network accordingly. Union Civil Aviation Minister Ram Mohan Naidu Kinjarapu today said that the IndiGo crisis was driven by problems in its crew rostering and internal planning system. Addressing the Rajya Sabha, Naidu said that strict Civil Aviation Requirements CARs are in place for passengers who have faced difficulties due to delays and cancellations. I want more players in the industry. Today, India has a capacity of five big airlines and there has been an effort from the ministry to encourage more airlines, he added. UBS kept its Buy call on the shares of IndiGo, but reduced its target price for the stock to Rs 6,350 per share. This implies an upside potential of more than 18 percent from the stocks previous closing price. The international brokerage said that inadequate preparations for the revised FDTL norms have led to major disruptions. It raised cost estimates for FY26-FY28 to account for the additional crew required to comply with the FDTL norms and higher operational costs driven by rupee depreciation against the dollar. IndiGos long-term growth outlook however remains robust, supported by its international expansion, UBS said. It added that the key downside risks include any contingent costs arising from operational disruptions and further depreciation. Jefferies kept a Buy call on the stock, with a target price of Rs 7,025 per share. This implies an upside potential of nearly 31 percent from the stocks previous closing price. The international brokerage noted that the company has been hit the hardest by the new FDTL norms, which reduce pilot duty hours and increases crew requirements. It noted that the rule change coincided with IndiGos capacity expansion, technical issues and congestion, triggering cascading disruptions. Airline is now recalibrating schedules and expects normalcy by mid-December, Jefferies noted, adding that IndiGo will face rising costs from disruptions and higher crew expenses. JM Financial kept a Reduce call on the stock, with a target price of Rs 5,570 apiece. This implies an upside potential of around 4 percent from the stocks previous closing price. The domestic brokerage said that recent mismanagement leading to significant flight cancellations is largely a function of new FDTL norms impact kicking in immediately post Airbus software upgrade challenges. The recent incident is likely to lead to a higher CAGR in CASK ex-fuel-ex-forex in future years subject to regulatory actions, it said. JM Financial noted that the show-cause notice sent to the CEO is likely to further dampen stock performance besides possible impending one-time penalty. Near-term, we estimate earnings hit of 8-9% for FY26 if the situation lasts for a total of 15 days. We await further clarity to revise our earnings estimates, given its a developing situation. Even as the FY26 earnings hit has been priced in, the stock is yet to price in 1 structural cost increase driven by regulatory actions 2 one time penalty 3 management change if any, it added. IndiGo shares have fallen more than 13 percent in the past five days, and around 10 percent in the past one month. The shares of the airline have fallen more than 12 percent in the past six months, but are up nearly 9 percent in 2025 so far. The stocks PE ratio currently stands at around 31. Title: Biocon merger is earnings dilutive, avoid EMS sector for now, says Dharmesh Kant
Content: Market expert Dharmesh Kant has voiced a cautious outlook on Biocon following its recent merger, and has recommended avoiding the electronics manufacturing services (EMS) sector for the time being. Speaking with CNBC TV18, Dharmesh Kant, Head Research at Chola Securities, said that while the street may have anticipated the move to make Biocon Biologics a 100% subsidiary, the deal is likely to be dilutive to earnings per share (EPS). Delving into the Biocon deal, Kant pointed out that the company has historically been 'over-hyped', with its performance not always matching expectations. He highlighted that over the last decade, Biocon's profitability growth has been modest, at around 9-10%, while its return on equity (ROE) has remained in the mid-single digits. He believes the current merger is not value accretive. "With this merger coming into play, it's not that it's value accretive or EPS accretive, I think it's EPS dilutive," he stated. The dilution is expected to come from two primary sources: the upcoming qualified institutional placement (QIP) and an increased debt burden that will lead to higher expenses. According to his analysis, it could take a year to a year and a half for the synergies from the merger to fully materialise. He also suggested that the company pursued this route to prevent 'value dilution' that might have occurred with an initial public offering (IPO). Consequently, Kant anticipates a correction in Biocon's stock, which he believes could persist for about a year until the company demonstrates a return to a double-digit growth trajectory. Shifting focus to the EMS space, the expert addressed the recent pressure on stocks like Kaynes Technology and PG Electroplast. He clarified that the issue is not isolated but rather a sector-wide phenomenon. "There has been a deceleration in the entire EMS space that we have seen, be it PG Electroplast or the others in the play like Kaynes, Dixon, Amber. Everybody is facing the heat of decelerating business growth trajectory," he observed. Two major headwinds for the sector are uncomfortable valuations, which he described as 'pretty high', and the prospect of intensifying competition. He specifically mentioned the potential for increased competition from Larsen & Toubro (L&T) as it plans a significant foray into the EMS market in the coming years. For PG Electroplast in particular, a significant factor is the pending approval for a technology transfer tie-up with a Chinese firm for air conditioner compressor technology. He noted that if this permission is granted, it could be a 'different story' for the company, as this technology is currently elusive for Indian manufacturers. However, pending this development, his overall call for the EMS sector is one of avoidance. He suggested that while some stocks might see a bounce-back, it would likely be a temporary rebound rather than a structural recovery, advising investors to stay away from the space for some time.

cleaned_text: Market expert Dharmesh Kant has voiced a cautious outlook on Biocon following its recent merger, and has recommended avoiding the electronics manufacturing services EMS sector for the time being. Speaking with CNBC TV18, Dharmesh Kant, Head Research at Chola Securities, said that while the street may have anticipated the move to make Biocon Biologics a 100% subsidiary, the deal is likely to be dilutive to earnings per share EPS. Delving into the Biocon deal, Kant pointed out that the company has historically been over-hyped, with its performance not always matching expectations. He highlighted that over the last decade, Biocons profitability growth has been modest, at around 9-10%, while its return on equity ROE has remained in the mid-single digits. He believes the current merger is not value accretive. With this merger coming into play, its not that its value accretive or EPS accretive, I think its EPS dilutive, he stated. The dilution is expected to come from two primary sources the upcoming qualified institutional placement QIP and an increased debt burden that will lead to higher expenses. According to his analysis, it could take a year to a year and a half for the synergies from the merger to fully materialise. He also suggested that the company pursued this route to prevent value dilution that might have occurred with an initial public offering IPO. Consequently, Kant anticipates a correction in Biocons stock, which he believes could persist for about a year until the company demonstrates a return to a double-digit growth trajectory. Shifting focus to the EMS space, the expert addressed the recent pressure on stocks like Kaynes Technology and PG Electroplast. He clarified that the issue is not isolated but rather a sector-wide phenomenon. There has been a deceleration in the entire EMS space that we have seen, be it PG Electroplast or the others in the play like Kaynes, Dixon, Amber. Everybody is facing the heat of decelerating business growth trajectory, he observed. Two major headwinds for the sector are uncomfortable valuations, which he described as pretty high, and the prospect of intensifying competition. He specifically mentioned the potential for increased competition from Larsen Toubro LT as it plans a significant foray into the EMS market in the coming years. For PG Electroplast in particular, a significant factor is the pending approval for a technology transfer tie-up with a Chinese firm for air conditioner compressor technology. He noted that if this permission is granted, it could be a different story for the company, as this technology is currently elusive for Indian manufacturers. However, pending this development, his overall call for the EMS sector is one of avoidance. He suggested that while some stocks might see a bounce-back, it would likely be a temporary rebound rather than a structural recovery, advising investors to stay away from the space for some time.

Title: MC EXCLUSIVE      ICICI Prudential AMC to launch three SIF products; CEO Nimesh Shah sees opportunity, not cannibalisation
Content: ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company is preparing a series of fund launches under the newly created, SEBI-approved SIF category, with Managing Director and CEO Nimesh Shah expressing optimism about its long-term potential while emphasising that early traction will take time. He was speaking during an exclusive interaction with Moneycontrol at the AMC’s bumper IPO launch. The issue will be a 100 percent OFS of up to 9.91 percent of the equity share capital. ICICI Prudential AMC is a joint venture of ICICI Bank and Prudential Corporation Holdings Limited. It is currently the second-largest AMC by AUM and the sixth AMC to go public. The price band has been fixed at Rs 2,061–2,165 per share, valuing the company at around Rs 10,600 crore at the top end. The issue will open on December 12 and close on December 16. Speaking about the SIF category, Shah said SEBI “has thought through the SIF category very well,” adding that the segment holds significant long-term promise. However, he cautioned against expecting immediate scale. “It will happen. I don’t expect that something will happen in 6 months, 1 year,” he noted. Currently, around four mutual funds have launched SIF products, including Edelweiss Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, ITI AMC and Quant AMC, among others. ICICI Prudential AMC currently has a 13.2 percent market share and reported a profit of Rs 1,618 crore and revenue of Rs 2,949 crore in the six months ended September 2025—up 21.9 percent and 20 percent respectively from a year earlier. For the financial year ended March 2025, profit rose 29.3 percent to Rs 2,651 crore, while revenue surged 32.4 percent to Rs 4,977 crore. The firm manages 143 mutual fund schemes, the highest among domestic asset managers. Other AMCs in the listed space include HDFC AMC, Nippon Life India Asset Management, UTI AMC, Canara Robeco AMC and Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC. Follow all IPO news here.

cleaned_text: ICICI Prudential Asset Management Company is preparing a series of fund launches under the newly created, SEBI-approved SIF category, with Managing Director and CEO Nimesh Shah expressing optimism about its long-term potential while emphasising that early traction will take time. He was speaking during an exclusive interaction with Moneycontrol at the AMCs bumper IPO launch. The issue will be a 100 percent OFS of up to 9.91 percent of the equity share capital. ICICI Prudential AMC is a joint venture of ICICI Bank and Prudential Corporation Holdings Limited. It is currently the second-largest AMC by AUM and the sixth AMC to go public. The price band has been fixed at Rs 2,0612,165 per share, valuing the company at around Rs 10,600 crore at the top end. The issue will open on December 12 and close on December 16. Speaking about the SIF category, Shah said SEBI has thought through the SIF category very well, adding that the segment holds significant long-term promise. However, he cautioned against expecting immediate scale. It will happen. I dont expect that something will happen in 6 months, 1 year, he noted. Currently, around four mutual funds have launched SIF products, including Edelweiss Mutual Fund, SBI Mutual Fund, ITI AMC and Quant AMC, among others. ICICI Prudential AMC currently has a 13.2 percent market share and reported a profit of Rs 1,618 crore and revenue of Rs 2,949 crore in the six months ended September 2025up 21.9 percent and 20 percent respectively from a year earlier. For the financial year ended March 2025, profit rose 29.3 percent to Rs 2,651 crore, while revenue surged 32.4 percent to Rs 4,977 crore. The firm manages 143 mutual fund schemes, the highest among domestic asset managers. Other AMCs in the listed space include HDFC AMC, Nippon Life India Asset Management, UTI AMC, Canara Robeco AMC and Aditya Birla Sun Life AMC. Follow all IPO news here.
